notesStmt.note: This manuscript was written sometime after the date of the letter on the reverse (September 25, 1889) and before October 18, 1890, the date on which Whitman sent the finished poem to the editor of Harper's Magazine (see Whitman's note on a later draft of the poem).

"The Unexpress'd" was first published in the March 1891 issue of Lippincott's Magazine in a group of four poems under the collective title "Old-Age Echoes." It later appeared, ungrouped, in Good-Bye My Fancy (1891).

lg.head: The Unexpress'd
lg.l: How dare one say it? yet
After the cycles, poems, singers, plays,

Vaunted Ionia's, India's—Homer, Shak-
spereShakspere
—all—times ‸dotted roads, areas,

The ‸retrospective clusters and the Milky Ways of stars
—rhythm's Nature's, pulses, reap'd,
All ‸retrospective passions, heros, war, love, adoration

All the ages' plummets sent down dropt
down to their utmost depths,

All lives, throats, brains, hopes—all experiences
rising?risen to utterance

And But yet something ye yet yet left? unexpress'd unsung, never not yet told put out in song nor print
perhaps?
Maybe the best yet ‸ unsung left un unexpress'd ‸and lacking?
All the good songs, or long or short, all tongues all lands

But something yet unsung—not put
yet in voice or print—something lacking?
